claim: `check-reaches-a-path-through-the-index` cannot be widened to judge a page's test fixtures, because the check names a page wherever the index knows a page ending with the path spelled, and a fixtures file spells short paths into a tree it invents rather than into this one. Closing the hole the widening aimed at takes a narrower rule matching a whole path rather than a suffix, which is a redesign of the check rather than a widening of its reach.

evidence:
A fixture builds a small tree of its own and spells paths into that tree. Those paths are short, so the suffix rule the check states matches a real page almost every time. The fixtures beside `rooting.module.test.ts` spell `cli/cli.module.code.ts`, and the check names the page at `command/modules/cli/cli.module.code.ts`, which the fixture never meant.

The widening landed as `aad3381d614`, and an audit of the check over the whole tree then answered `1 check answered for aad3381d61443031ff27fc625bbe159e462b6efd, and 141 refusals in all`. Counting the literals that exactly equal a tracked path had predicted 17. The gap between 17 and 141 is the suffix rule firing on invented paths.

Every refusal becomes ratchet debt for whichever seat next touches that file, so the widening would have charged 141 files to every other seat for a hole nobody had hit. It was reverted at `8949f12afd9`.

The hole the widening aimed at is real: a captured fixture holding a path a move respelled goes stale with nothing judging it. Catching that wants the check to match a literal against a whole path rather than against any page ending with it, and to run that narrower rule on fixtures alone.
